reason: This passage (Exodus 14) depicts the crossing of the Red Sea and Pharaoh's pursuit. While the Egyptian Pharaoh and his officials complain about letting the Israelites go (וַיֹּֽאמרוּ מַה־ זֹּ֣את עָשִׂ֔ינוּ), and the Israelite people themselves complain to Moses about their circumstances, there are no Hebrew leaders complaining about the Hebrew people. Instead, Moses (the Hebrew leader) responds to the people's complaints with encouragement, telling them not to be afraid and to witness God's salvation. The Hebrew leadership does not lodge complaints against the people in this text.
story: The Pharaoh chases after the Hebrews
